correctness.rationale: With column coordinates and χ(x,y)=xᵗAy, Serre duality gives AS*=Aᵗ, and the shift by 3 gives T*=−A⁻ᵗA. The geometric-helix input is substantive: Loginov–Orlov give the periodic standard helix and state in the proof of Proposition 3.7 that the right dual of a full geometric helix also generates a geometric helix. For p>0 this kills the nonzero-degree Hom terms; for p=0 exceptionality suffices. Independent exact matrix replay from both printed matrices, without running the uploaded script, computed N=T*−I and found N⁴=0 for each. For the four right-dual terms the diagonals of ANᵏ, k=0,1,2,3, give the tuples (1,38,108,72), (1,146,432,288), (1,146,432,288), (1,38,108,72); they give (1,38,108,72) for every standard term. The binomial identity therefore proves the cubics for every integer p≥0, not just samples. Multiplying the resulting series by (1−t)^4 gives the displayed numerators (1,35,35,1) and (1,143,143,1). Both functions equal 1 at p=0; the claim is two distinct functions. Reviewed frozen RESULT.md lines 85–150, VERIFICATION.md, verify.py and VERIFY.txt; the matrix replay verifies pairings and does not replace the geometric-helix input.
